title: JockeyBench: The Racing Analyst's Last Exam
abstract: arXiv:2610.19589v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Evaluating LLM agents in noisy sequential forecasting is challenging: strong performance may reflect a capable initial predictor rather than successful online revision, while accurate forecasts may still fail to deliver economic value after costs and market frictions. Existing benchmarks rarely isolate revision gains, compare reusable model-written predictors with direct LLM forecasting on the same tasks, or assess forecast quality alongside research costs and realized returns. To address these gaps, we introduce JockeyBench, a leakage-controlled replay benchmark built from 12 years of Japanese horse-racing records. Agents acquire evidence at a cost and seal probabilistic forecasts before outcomes are revealed. To isolate the effect of revision, we pair each adaptive code-as-policy agent with a frozen copy of its initial predictor. translated_title: JockeyBench：赛马分析师的终极考试
translated_abstract: 在噪声环境下的顺序预测任务中评估LLM智能体颇具挑战性：强劲的表现可能仅反映出一个有能力的初始预测器，而非成功的在线修正；同时，即使预测准确，在扣除成本和市场摩擦之后，也可能无法带来实际的经济价值。现有基准很少能分离出修正带来的收益，很少在同一任务上将可复用的模型生成预测器与直接的LLM预测进行比较，也很少将预测质量与研究成本和实际收益结合起来评估。为弥补这些空白，我们推出了JockeyBench，这是一个基于12年日本赛马记录构建的、严格控制信息泄漏的回放基准。在该基准中，智能体需付出成本获取证据，并在结果揭晓之前封存其概率预测。为了分离出修正行为的效果，我们将每个自适应的“代码即策略”智能体与其初始预测器的冻结副本进行配对对比。我们还将执行可复用预测程序的“代码即策略”方法与“LLM即策略”方法进行比较。
tldr: 提出了JockeyBench——一个基于12年日本赛马记录、严格控制信息泄漏的回放基准，通过将自适应智能体与其冻结的初始预测器配对来分离在线修正的真实收益，并比较代码即策略与LLM即策略两种范式，同时综合评估预测质量、研究成本与实际经济回报。
en_tdlr: JockeyBench, a leakage-controlled replay benchmark built from 12 years of Japanese horse-racing records, isolates the true gains of online revision by pairing adaptive agents with frozen copies of their initial predictors, and compares code-as-policy with LLM-as-policy while jointly assessing forecast quality, research costs, and realized economic returns.
